t: Start on all fours in a quadruped position, with your hands directly under your shoulders and your knees directly under your hips. | Set your wrists, knees, and shins firmly on the floor, and keep your spine in a flat, neutral position to begin. | Inhale gently to prepare, keeping your neck long and your head in line with your spine. | As you exhale, slowly round your back upward toward the ceiling, drawing your belly button in and tucking your chin toward your chest. | Continue arching until you feel a comfortable stretch along your spine and back muscles, without forcing the range. | Hold the rounded position briefly, breathing steadily and feeling the stretch through your erector spinae. | Inhale as you slowly release back to the flat, neutral starting position with control. | Repeat for the desired number of slow, controlled repetitions.

t: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart, chest up, and core gently braced. | Shift your weight onto your left foot and drive your right knee up toward your chest in a controlled, deliberate motion. | At the same time, raise both arms in an upbeat, celebratory motion to add rhythm and momentum. | Lower your right foot back to the floor under control and return your arms to your sides. | Repeat on the other side, driving your left knee up while keeping your torso upright. | Find a steady, repeatable rhythm and continue alternating knees for your target time or rep count. | To progress, add a light hop on the standing leg as you drive the knee; to regress, step the knee up without leaving the ground. | Finish by slowing the pace, then bring both feet together and let your breathing settle.

t: Stand facing a sturdy chair, an arm's length away, with your feet hip-width apart and your weight evenly balanced. | Lift one leg and place your heel on the seat of the chair, keeping that knee straight and your toes pointing up toward you. | Square your hips so both hip bones face forward and keep your standing leg slightly soft, not locked. | Straighten your spine and lengthen through the crown of your head before you move. | Hinge forward from your hips, sliding your hands down the raised leg until you feel a gentle stretch along the back of the thigh. | Stop at the first point of mild tension, keeping your back flat rather than rounding your shoulders. | Hold the position for 20–30 seconds while breathing slowly and steadily. | Ease back upright, lower your foot to the floor, then repeat on the other leg.

t: Start in a high plank with your wrists stacked under your shoulders, fingers spread, and your body in one straight line from head to heels. | Engage your core, draw your shoulder blades down your back, and press the floor away to keep your upper back broad. | Shift your weight forward on an inhale so your shoulders move slightly past your wrists and you come onto the balls of your feet. | Exhale and bend your elbows straight back, keeping them tucked close to your ribs rather than flaring out to the sides. | Lower under control until your upper arms are roughly parallel to the floor and your elbows are bent close to 90°, holding your body in one line. | Hover here with your gaze slightly forward, keeping your hips level with your shoulders and your legs active. | Hold for a breath, then either lower all the way down or roll forward over your toes and press into upward-facing dog to continue the flow. | To exit, release your knees and chest to the mat or press back up to plank with control.

t: Set up two sturdy, stable benches roughly a body-length apart and check that neither will slide before you load them. | Sit between them and place your upper back and the tops of your shoulders on one bench, with the back of your head supported or relaxed neutral. | Rest your heels on the second bench, legs straight, so your body is suspended over the gap. | Brace your core, squeeze your glutes, and lift your hips until your body forms one straight line from shoulders to heels. | Hold this rigid position, breathing steadily, without letting your hips sag toward the floor or pike upward. | Keep your neck neutral and avoid arching your lower back or pushing your chin up to overextend. | Hold for your target time, then lower your hips under control and sit back down between the benches to finish.

t: Sit or stand tall with your spine long, shoulders relaxed and down, and your gaze straight ahead. | Take a slow breath in, then exhale and gently nod your head forward, lowering your chin toward your chest. | Let the weight of your head do the work — avoid pulling or forcing — until you feel a light, comfortable stretch along the back of your neck. | Keep your shoulders relaxed and your jaw loose so the stretch stays in the neck and upper spine. | Hold the position for 15–30 seconds, breathing slowly and evenly throughout. | To deepen it slightly, you may rest your fingertips lightly on the back of your head, but never pull hard. | Slowly raise your head back to a neutral, upright position to finish. | Repeat for 2–3 gentle holds, easing off the moment you feel any pinching or pain.

t: Grip the pull-up bar with an underhand (supinated) grip about shoulder-width apart, wrapping your thumbs around the bar. | Hang from the bar with your arms fully extended, shoulders engaged, and core braced to limit swinging. | Pull yourself up by driving your elbows down and back, leading with your chest toward the bar. | Continue pulling past the normal top position, raising your chin and head up and over the bar. | Tilt your head slightly back as you clear the bar, keeping your neck relaxed and your shoulders stable. | Pause briefly at the top with the bar below your chin, staying in control. | Lower yourself slowly and under control until your arms are fully extended again. | Reset your hang, then repeat for reps before dropping off the bar safely.

t: Stand tall with your feet about shoulder-width apart and cup your hands together at chest height, elbows tucked, as if cradling a goblet against your sternum. | Brace your core, keep your chest up, and squat straight down at the 12 o'clock (neutral) position until your thighs are roughly parallel to the floor. | Drive through your mid-foot to stand back up, keeping your hands fixed at your chest throughout. | Step your lead foot out toward the 3 o'clock position to widen and angle your stance, then squat down and return to standing. | Reset to center, then step toward the 6 o'clock position (a longer stance) and perform another controlled squat. | Reset again and step toward the 9 o'clock position to mirror the 3 o'clock angle, squatting and standing with control. | Return your feet to center to complete one full clock circuit, keeping your torso upright the whole time. | Repeat the circuit for your target reps, then lower your hands and stand tall to finish.

t: Set up in a high plank with your hands slightly wider than shoulder-width, fingers forward, and your body in a straight line from head to heels. | Brace your core and squeeze your glutes so your hips neither sag nor pike up. | Bend your elbows and lower your chest toward the floor, keeping your elbows at roughly a 45° angle to your torso. | Press back up to full arm extension to complete one push-up at the 12 o'clock position. | Keeping one hand planted as the pivot, step the other hand a short arc clockwise to the next clock position, resetting into a solid plank. | Perform another full push-up at the new angle, then walk the hand to the next position and repeat. | Continue around the clock until you complete the circle, then reverse direction or rest. | Lower your knees to finish the set and shake out your wrists and shoulders.

t: Set out your cones (or any small markers) in the pattern you want to run — common layouts are a straight line, an L-shape, or three cones spaced 5 yards apart. | Start in an athletic stance at the first cone: feet shoulder-width apart, knees bent, weight on the balls of your feet, and hips low. | Drive off explosively toward the next cone, keeping your steps short and quick rather than long and floaty. | As you reach each cone, drop your hips and decelerate under control, planting your outside foot to change direction. | Push off the planted foot to accelerate toward the next marker, staying low through the turn. | Pump your arms in rhythm with your legs to drive speed and keep your balance through each cut. | Complete the full pattern at a controlled but brisk pace, touching or rounding each cone as your layout requires. | Walk back to the start to recover, then repeat for the planned number of runs.

t: Start in a high plank with your hands slightly wider than shoulder-width and your body in a straight line from head to heels. | Brace your core and set your shoulder blades down and back to stabilize your trunk. | Bend your elbows to lower your chest toward the floor, keeping them tucked at roughly a 45° angle to your torso. | As you descend, rotate your hips and torso and drive one knee diagonally across your body toward the opposite elbow. | Pause briefly near the bottom with the knee drawn in and your chest just above the floor. | Reverse the twist, returning the foot to the plank position as you press back up to full arm extension. | Repeat the rotation to the same side or alternate sides each rep, keeping your hips from sagging throughout. | Finish your reps and lower your knees to the floor to rest.

t: Stand tall on one leg with your working foot flat and your other knee bent so the rear foot floats just behind you. | Extend your arms straight out in front of you at roughly shoulder height to act as a counterbalance. You can hold a very light plate or dumbbell in your hands if you want more reach. | Brace your core, keep your chest up, and set your standing knee tracking over your toes. | Hinge at the hips and bend your standing knee to lower under control, letting your rear leg trail back and down behind you. | Descend until your rear knee lightly taps the floor, keeping most of your weight through the heel and mid-foot of your standing leg. | Drive through your standing foot and extend the hip and knee to stand back up, keeping your arms reaching forward for balance. | Complete all reps on one leg, then switch sides and repeat.

t: Stand tall with your feet about hip- to shoulder-width apart and your weight balanced over the middle of your feet. | Place both hands firmly on your hips and keep them there for the entire jump. | Dip down quickly into a quarter squat, bending at your hips, knees, and ankles in one smooth countermovement. | Without pausing at the bottom, drive your feet hard into the floor and explode straight up. | Fully extend your hips, knees, and ankles at the top so your body reaches a tall, straight line in the air. | Spot the floor as you descend and land softly on the balls of your feet, then your whole foot. | Absorb the landing by bending your hips, knees, and ankles back into a controlled quarter squat. | Reset to a tall stance with your hands still on your hips, then repeat for the prescribed reps.

t: Stand tall with your feet about shoulder-width apart, weight balanced over the middle of your feet, and your arms hanging relaxed at your sides. | Brace your core and keep your chest up while looking straight ahead at a fixed point. | Drop into a fast countermovement by bending your hips, knees, and ankles into a quarter-squat as your arms swing back behind your hips. | Without pausing at the bottom, reverse direction explosively and extend your hips, knees, and ankles to drive straight up. | Pull your arms forcefully upward and overhead in time with the jump to add momentum and maximize height. | Reach full extension at the top, with your body straight and your feet leaving the ground together. | Land softly on the balls of your feet first, then settle through your whole foot, bending your hips and knees to absorb the impact. | Reset to a tall stance, regain your balance, and repeat for the prescribed number of reps.

t: Sit on the floor with your legs extended and your spine tall. | Bend your right knee and cross it over your left, stacking your right knee directly on top of your left so both knees line up at the center. | Draw both heels in toward opposite hips and let your sitting bones settle evenly on the floor. | Reach your right arm overhead, bend the elbow, and let your right hand drop down between your shoulder blades. | Sweep your left arm behind your back and bend the elbow upward so your left hand climbs toward your right. | Clasp your fingers together between your shoulder blades, keeping your chest lifted and your top elbow pointing toward the ceiling. | Breathe slowly and hold for 30 to 60 seconds, easing into the shoulder and hip stretch without forcing. | Release the bind gently, unstack your legs, then repeat with the opposite arm on top and the opposite knee stacked.

t: Set up on all fours on a mat in a quadruped position, with your wrists stacked under your shoulders and your knees under your hips. | Spread your fingers wide and press evenly through your palms, keeping your spine in a neutral, flat starting position. | Inhale slowly and let your belly drop toward the floor as you tilt your pelvis so your tailbone lifts upward. | Lift your chest and gaze gently forward and up, allowing your shoulder blades to draw down your back. | Continue the gentle arch through your mid and lower spine without forcing the movement or cranking your neck back. | Hold the extended position for a breath or two, feeling the stretch across your abdomen and the openness through your spine. | Exhale and return to the neutral flat-back position, or flow directly into the cat stretch by rounding your spine. | Repeat for several slow, breath-paced reps, then finish back in a neutral quadruped position.

t: Sit on the floor with your knees bent, feet flat, and hands placed behind your hips with your fingers pointing toward your heels. | Press through your hands and feet to lift your hips off the floor until your torso and thighs form a flat, tabletop line. | Let your head fall back gently and keep your shoulders pulled down away from your ears. | Drive your hips a little higher and squeeze your glutes to deepen the stretch across the front of your torso. | Feel the lengthening through your abdominals, hips, and shoulders, and hold the position with steady breathing. | Hold for 20–40 seconds, breathing slowly and keeping your core lightly engaged. | Lower your hips back to the floor under control to finish the stretch.

t: Sit on the floor with your knees bent, feet flat and hip-width apart, and your hands planted behind you with fingers pointing toward your heels. | Press through your hands and feet to lift your hips off the floor until your torso forms a flat tabletop, roughly parallel to the ground. | Brace your core and squeeze your glutes to hold your hips high and level — this is your starting position. | Step forward by moving your opposite hand and foot together, then the other hand and foot, staying low and controlled. | Keep your hips lifted throughout; avoid letting them sag toward the floor between steps. | Travel the planned distance forward, then reverse the pattern to walk backward to your start. | To work laterally, step both hands and feet to one side, then the other, keeping your chest open and shoulders stable. | Lower your hips to the floor under control to finish the set.

t: Squat down with your feet close together and place both hands flat on the floor shoulder-width apart, fingers spread wide. | Spread your fingers and grip the mat lightly, keeping your wrists, hands, and forearms set as a stable base. | Bend your elbows slightly back, as in a low push-up, to create a shelf for your knees on the backs of your upper arms. | Rise onto the balls of your feet and place your knees high up onto your upper arms, as close to your armpits as you can. | Shift your weight forward over your hands until your feet feel light and your gaze moves to the floor just ahead of your fingers. | Lift one foot and then the other off the floor, drawing your heels in toward your hips and rounding your upper back. | Balance with your knees squeezing your arms, hips lifted, and arms gradually straightening as much as is comfortable. | Hold for a few steady breaths, then lower your feet back to the floor with control and return to a squat.

t: Clear enough floor space and start on all fours in a bear-crawl position: hands under shoulders, knees under hips and hovering just off the floor, back flat and core braced. | Keeping your hips low, take a small step with one hand and the opposite foot to crawl a short distance forward, staying controlled and quiet. | To switch sides, lift one hand off the floor and rotate your hips and chest toward the ceiling, reaching that hand behind you to plant it. | Follow the rotation by turning your feet so you land in a crab position: hands behind your hips with fingers pointing toward your feet, feet flat, and hips lifted into a reverse tabletop. | Drive through your heels and palms to push your hips up, hold the crab briefly, then crawl backward a short distance keeping your hips elevated. | Reverse the movement by rotating your hips and chest back toward the floor and stepping a hand under your shoulder to return to the bear-crawl position. | Continue alternating smoothly between crawl and crab for the prescribed time or reps, keeping the transitions fluid and your core engaged throughout. | To finish, return to the bear-crawl position, then lower your knees and stand up under control.

t: Start standing tall at the top of your mat with your feet together and your weight evenly balanced. | Step your right foot back into a long lunge, keeping the front (left) knee stacked directly over the ankle and the back leg straight or with a soft bend. | Lower your hips toward the floor until you feel a gentle stretch through the front of the back hip and thigh, keeping the front knee at roughly 90 degrees. | Inhale and sweep both arms up alongside your ears, palms facing in or lightly touching, and lengthen up through your fingertips. | Lift your chest and gently arch back, drawing your shoulder blades down and keeping your lower ribs from flaring as you reach up and slightly back. | Hold the pose for 20 to 30 seconds, breathing steadily and keeping your core lightly engaged to support your lower back. | To release, lower your arms, step your back foot forward to meet the front, and return to standing. | Repeat on the other side, stepping the left foot back to balance both hips.

t: Set up under a sturdy pull-up bar that you can reach with a small jump or step, ideally one that lets your feet clear the floor at full hang. | Grip the bar with both hands roughly shoulder-width apart, palms facing away, and wrap your thumbs around the bar for a secure hold. | Step or hop off and let your body hang with your arms fully straight, allowing your shoulders to relax up toward your ears. | Keep your legs relaxed and let your body settle, breathing slowly as your lats and shoulders decompress under your own body weight. | Once comfortable, gently draw your shoulder blades down and back for a few seconds to engage the lower and middle traps, then relax again into the passive hang. | Hold the position for 20 to 60 seconds, staying calm and avoiding any swinging or kipping. | To finish, place your feet back on the floor or a box, take the weight off your arms before releasing the bar, and step down with control.

t: Set a loaded barbell on the floor with the bar over your mid-foot, and stand with your feet about hip-width apart and toes turned slightly out. | Hinge at the hips by pushing your hips back and bending your knees, lowering your torso to grip the bar just outside your shins. | Before you pull, set the right hip position: lift your hips until your shins are roughly vertical and the bar is close to your legs, not so high that your knees lock early or so low that you turn the pull into a squat. | Brace by taking a deep breath into your belly and tightening your core, then pull the slack out of the bar so your hips, shoulders, and the bar are loaded together. | Drive the floor away through your thighs and push your hips forward, keeping the bar dragging up your shins and the bar path vertical. | Stand tall by fully extending your hips and knees at the same time, squeezing the glutes at the top without leaning back or hyperextending your lower back. | Lower the bar by pushing your hips back first, then bending the knees once the bar passes them, returning it to the floor under control. | Reset your brace and hip position before each rep, then re-rack or set the bar down safely when the set is finished.

t: Set up between sturdy parallel or dip bars, gripping one bar in each hand with your palms facing inward. | Press down through your hands to lift your feet off the floor, supporting your full bodyweight with your arms straight and locked. | Relax your shoulders and let them rise up toward your ears, allowing your body to sink slightly between the bars. | Feel the gentle stretch and decompression across the tops of your shoulders and your upper back. | Now actively depress your shoulders — pull your shoulder blades down and away from your ears without bending your elbows. | Hold the depressed position for 2–3 seconds, keeping your chest tall and your neck long. | Breathe slowly and cycle between the relaxed (shrugged) and the depressed position for the desired time. | Lower your feet gently back to the floor to finish, then step off the bars under control.

t: Stand tall with your feet about hip-width apart and your weight balanced evenly through both feet. | Brace your core lightly and let your right arm hang while you reach your left arm straight up overhead. | Keeping both feet flat on the floor, bend your torso diagonally to the right, sliding your right hand down your thigh as your left arm follows the line of the stretch. | Reach the fingertips of your left hand up and over toward the right until you feel a gentle lengthening down the left side of your torso. | Hold the position and breathe slowly, staying just shy of any sharp or pinching sensation. | Hold for 20 to 30 seconds, then return to standing under control. | Switch the overhead arm and repeat the bend to the opposite side, matching the time on each side.

t: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart, chest up, and hands relaxed at your sides or clasped in front of your chest for balance. | Brace your core and step one foot out and forward on a diagonal, at roughly a 45° angle from straight ahead. | Plant the lead foot flat and bend both knees to lower your hips, keeping your front knee tracking over your toes. | Descend until your front thigh is about parallel to the floor and your back knee drops toward the ground, keeping your torso tall. | Drive through the heel and midfoot of your lead leg to push back up and return to the starting position. | Repeat for your target reps, then switch and step out on the diagonal with the other leg. | Finish standing tall with both feet together and your core still braced.

t: Stand in an athletic stance with your feet roughly shoulder-width apart, knees soft, and weight on the balls of your feet. | Raise both fists to guard height beside your chin, elbows tucked in and core braced. | Drive your right fist forward and across your body on an upward diagonal toward your opposite shoulder line, rotating through your hips and trunk. | Pivot your right foot and turn your hips into the punch so the power comes from rotation, not just the arm. | Snap the fist back to guard along the same path, keeping your chin protected. | Repeat with your left fist on the mirror-image diagonal, rotating to the opposite side. | Alternate sides in a steady rhythm, staying light on your feet and breathing out with each punch. | Continue for the set time or rep count, then return to a relaxed guard to finish.

t: Start in a high plank with your hands flat on the floor under your chest and your feet about hip-width apart. | Slide your hands together so your index fingers and thumbs touch, forming a diamond or triangle shape beneath your sternum. | Brace your core and squeeze your erector spinae to lock your hips, spine, and head into one straight line from heels to crown. | Bend your elbows and lower your chest toward your hands under control, keeping your elbows tracking close to your sides rather than flaring wide. | Lower until your chest lightly touches or nearly touches the back of your hands, keeping your back flat throughout. | Press back up by extending your elbows, driving through your palms until your arms are fully straight. | Keep your hips level and your spine neutral at the top, then repeat for your target reps. | Finish your final rep, lower your knees to the floor, and rest.

t: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides with a slight bend in your elbows. | Brace your core and keep your shoulders pulled down and back so you isolate the deltoids rather than shrug. | Way 1 — front raise: lift both dumbbells straight in front of you to about shoulder height, then lower under control. | Way 2 — lateral raise: raise both dumbbells out to your sides until your arms reach shoulder height, leading with your elbows, then lower slowly. | Way 3 — rear/bent raise: hinge slightly at the hips and raise the dumbbells out to the sides with your torso leaning forward to target the rear delts, then lower. | Way 4 — hold: raise the dumbbells to shoulder height in your chosen plane and pause for a couple of seconds to build time under tension. | Keep each rep smooth — avoid swinging the weights up or letting them drop on the way down. | Complete your reps through all four positions, then set the dumbbells down with control.

t: Stand tall with a light dumbbell in each hand, feet about shoulder-width apart and knees soft. | Brace your core, keep a slight bend in your elbows, and let the dumbbells hang at your sides with palms facing in. | Raise both dumbbells straight out to the front to shoulder height (front raise), then lower them under control. | Raise both dumbbells out to the sides to shoulder height (lateral raise), keeping your wrists in line with your forearms, then lower them. | Hinge slightly forward at the hips and raise the dumbbells out to the sides for the rear-delt portion, squeezing your shoulder blades, then return. | Continue cycling through the remaining raise angles for the set, keeping each rep slow and controlled. | Complete the planned number of rounds, then lower the dumbbells to your sides and set them down with control.

t: Sit or stand tall holding a dumbbell in each hand at shoulder height, elbows in front of your body and palms facing your torso. | Brace your core, keep your chest up, and set your shoulder blades down to create a stable pressing base. | Press one dumbbell up while rotating that wrist outward, so the palm turns to face forward as the arm reaches overhead. | Finish with the arm fully extended overhead, palm facing forward, without locking the elbow harshly or shrugging the shoulder up. | Reverse the path under control: lower the dumbbell while rotating the wrist back so the palm faces you again at shoulder height. | Repeat the press and rotation with the other arm, keeping the resting dumbbell steady at shoulder height. | Continue alternating arms for your target reps, keeping the tempo controlled in both directions. | After your final rep, lower both dumbbells to your thighs or set them down with control.

t: Sit on the end of a flat bench with a dumbbell standing on each thigh, then kick the weights back as you lie down so they end up at shoulder height. | Plant your feet on the floor, pull your shoulder blades down and together against the bench, and press both dumbbells straight up until your arms are fully extended over your chest — this is the high start position. | Keeping one arm locked out at the top, lower the opposite dumbbell under control until it is level with your chest, with your elbow at roughly a 45–75° angle to your torso. | Press that dumbbell back up to lock-out, squeezing your chest at the top until both arms are extended again. | Repeat with the other arm, lowering it while the first stays pressed up at the top. | Continue alternating arms for the prescribed reps, keeping your wrists stacked over your elbows throughout. | When finished, lower both dumbbells under control to your chest, then set them down on your thighs or the floor — do not drop them out to the sides.

t: Stand tall with a dumbbell in each hand, feet about hip-width apart and the dumbbells resting against the front of your thighs. | Hinge at the hips and bend your knees slightly to lower the dumbbells to the hang position at mid-thigh, keeping your back flat, chest up, and shoulders over the weights. | Explosively extend your hips, knees, and ankles (triple extension), driving the dumbbells upward and shrugging hard as they rise. | As the dumbbells reach their peak, pull yourself under them and rotate your elbows quickly forward, catching them on your shoulders in a partial squat (the clean). | Stand fully upright out of the catch with the dumbbells racked on your shoulders, hips and knees locked out. | Dip straight down a few inches by bending your knees, keeping your torso vertical, then drive explosively to punch the dumbbells overhead. | Catch the dumbbells locked out overhead, often with one foot stepping forward and one back (split) or in a slight squat, then bring your feet back in line. | Stabilize overhead with arms fully extended, then lower the dumbbells under control to your shoulders and back to the hang to begin the next rep.

t: Kneel tall on a mat with both knees down, hips and torso stacked vertically over your knees, glutes squeezed and core braced. | Hold a dumbbell in each hand at shoulder height with your palms facing you and your elbows tucked in front of your chest. | Keeping your ribs down, begin pressing the dumbbells upward as you rotate your palms outward so they face forward at the midpoint. | Continue pressing overhead until your arms are fully extended and your palms face away from you, with the dumbbells stacked over your shoulders. | Pause briefly at the top without shrugging your shoulders up toward your ears or arching your lower back. | Lower the dumbbells under control, reversing the rotation so your palms turn back toward you as the weights return to shoulder height. | Reset your brace at the bottom and repeat for your target reps, keeping your hips locked and torso upright throughout. | Finish your set, then lower the dumbbells to your thighs and place them down safely on either side.

t: Kneel on the floor with your knees about hip-width apart and your hips stacked over your knees, keeping your torso tall. | Brace your core and squeeze your glutes so your spine stays neutral and your ribs stay down. | Hold one dumbbell with both hands in front of your chest, gripping the heads or the handle firmly. | Begin circling the dumbbell around your head, drawing it close behind your skull without dropping your chin or arching your lower back. | Continue the path around the back of your head and bring the dumbbell forward to complete one full circle. | Keep the movement slow and controlled, letting your shoulders move through their range rather than swinging the weight. | Complete your reps in one direction, then reverse and circle the dumbbell the other way. | Lower the dumbbell back to your chest and set it down safely with control.

t: Kneel or sit beside a flat bench and rest your working forearm along the bench so your wrist and hand hang off the edge. | Hold a dumbbell that is loaded on one side only, gripping it toward the loaded end so the weight creates a rotational pull. | Start with your palm facing down (pronated), letting the offset load gently rotate your wrist toward the floor. | Brace your forearm flat against the bench and keep your elbow still so the motion comes only from your forearm rotating. | Rotate your forearm to turn your palm up (supinate), lifting the loaded end of the dumbbell against gravity. | Pause briefly at the top with your palm fully turned up, feeling the contraction in your forearm. | Lower under control back to the palm-down start, resisting the weight through the full range. | Complete your reps, then switch the dumbbell to the other hand and repeat.

t: Stand tall holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides, palms facing your thighs, with a slight bend in your elbows. | Brace your core, keep your chest up, and let your shoulders settle down away from your ears. | Raise the dumbbells out to the sides until your arms reach roughly the midpoint between your hips and shoulder height. | Lower the dumbbells only partway back down, stopping before they return fully to your sides to keep tension on the side delts. | Drive the dumbbells back up through the same short arc, leading with your elbows rather than your hands. | Repeat these partial reps in a controlled rhythm, keeping your torso still and avoiding any swing. | Continue until you reach your target reps or muscular failure, then lower the dumbbells fully to your sides with control.

t: Set up in a high plank with your hands stacked under your shoulders, feet slightly wider than hip-width for a stable base. | Place a single dumbbell on the floor just outside one hand, lying within easy reach. | Brace your abs and squeeze your glutes so your hips and shoulders stay square to the floor. | Reach across with the opposite hand, grip the dumbbell, and drag it across the floor to the other side of your body. | Keep your hips level throughout the pass — resist the urge to twist or let one hip dip toward the floor. | Return that hand to its plank position and reset your shoulders before the next pass. | Reach across with the other hand and drag the dumbbell back to the starting side, repeating in a controlled rhythm. | Continue alternating for your target reps, then lower your knees to finish.

t: Lie on your side along a stable flat bench, supporting your head so your spine stays neutral, with a light dumbbell in your top hand. | Let the dumbbell hang down in front of your hips, palm facing toward your feet and your arm nearly straight. | Brace your core and keep your torso stacked so you do not roll forward or backward during the lift. | Sweep the dumbbell up and over your body in a wide arc, leading with a long, slightly bent arm. | Raise it until your hand points roughly toward the ceiling and you feel the rear and lateral shoulder working. | Pause briefly at the top, keeping the shoulder blade set and the movement controlled. | Lower the dumbbell back along the same arc to the start under control, resisting gravity the whole way. | Complete all reps on one side, then roll over and repeat with the other arm.

t: Set a dumbbell on the floor outside each foot and stand with your feet about hip-width apart, dumbbells resting at your sides. | Hinge at the hips and bend your knees to grip the dumbbells with a neutral grip, keeping your chest up, back flat, and shoulders slightly ahead of the weights. | Brace your core and begin the pull by driving through the floor with your legs, keeping the dumbbells close to your body. | As the dumbbells pass your knees, explosively extend your hips, knees, and ankles in one powerful movement (triple extension), shrugging your traps upward. | Pull yourself under the dumbbells, whipping your elbows forward and around so the weights rotate up onto the front of your shoulders. | Catch the dumbbells at shoulder height in a quarter-squat with elbows high and your torso upright. | Stand fully erect to finish the rep with the dumbbells racked on your shoulders. | Lower the dumbbells under control back to your sides, then to the floor, and reset your setup before the next rep.

t: Set the preacher bench pad so the top sits just under your armpit, and pick up a dumbbell in one hand. | Sit and turn your torso slightly so you face the bench at an angle, resting the back of your working upper arm flat against the pad. | Let the arm extend down the pad to a near-full stretch, holding the dumbbell with a supinated (palm-up) grip and your wrist neutral. | Brace your core and keep your shoulder pinned to the pad so only the elbow moves. | Curl the dumbbell up toward your shoulder by flexing at the elbow, exhaling as you lift. | Squeeze at the top for a moment without letting your elbow drift off the pad. | Lower the dumbbell under control over two to three seconds back to the stretched starting position. | Finish all reps on one arm, then switch the dumbbell to the other hand and repeat.

t: Place two dumbbells on the floor shoulder-width apart, parallel to each other, with the handles lined up so they sit stable under your hands. | Grip the dumbbell handles and set up in a high plank with hands under your shoulders, wrists neutral, and your body in a straight line from head to heels. | Brace your core and squeeze your glutes so your hips neither sag nor pike up. | Bend your elbows and lower your chest toward the floor between the dumbbells, keeping your elbows at roughly a 45-degree angle to your torso. | Press back up through your hands until your arms are fully extended, returning to the top plank position. | From the top, shift your weight onto one supporting hand, lift the opposite dumbbell off the floor, and raise it straight out in front of you to about shoulder height with a slight bend in the elbow. | Lower the dumbbell back to the floor under control and reset your hand on the handle. | Perform the next push-up, then raise the dumbbell on the opposite side, alternating arms each round. | Continue for your target reps, then lower your knees and set both dumbbells down to finish.

t: Place two dumbbells shoulder-width apart on the floor and grip one in each hand, wrists stacked under your shoulders. | Walk your feet back into a high-plank position with your legs wide for a stable base and your hips level. | Brace your core hard so your torso and hips stay square to the floor, not twisting toward either side. | Row one dumbbell to your ribs by driving the elbow up and back, keeping it close to your body while the opposite arm presses the floor. | Lower the dumbbell under control and repeat the row on the other side, resisting any rotation through your waist. | Take a small step forward with the same-side hand and foot, then move the dumbbell with that hand to travel one stride ahead. | Step the other hand and foot forward to bring the second dumbbell level, returning to a stable plank. | Continue alternating rows and forward steps for the prescribed distance or reps, then carefully set the dumbbells down.

t: Set an incline bench to roughly 30–45° and grab a dumbbell in each hand with an underhand grip, palms facing forward. | Lie face-down on the bench with your chest and stomach against the pad and your feet planted for stability. | Let your arms hang straight down toward the floor, holding the dumbbells with your palms facing away from the bench. | Pull your shoulder blades down and back, then row the dumbbells up by driving your elbows toward your hips. | Keep your elbows close to your sides and bring the dumbbells toward your lower ribs until your upper arms pass your torso. | Squeeze your back at the top, holding the contraction briefly without shrugging your shoulders up. | Lower the dumbbells under control until your arms are fully extended and your shoulder blades stretch forward. | Complete your reps, then sit up and set the dumbbells down with control.

nH: Dumbbell Reverse Grip Squeeze Bench Press
t: Sit on a flat bench holding a dumbbell in each hand, then lie back and bring the dumbbells together over your chest. | Rotate your hands to a reverse, underhand grip so your palms face toward your feet, and press the two dumbbells flat against each other. | Set your feet firmly on the floor and pull your shoulder blades down and together against the bench. | Lower the dumbbells under control toward your lower chest, keeping your elbows tucked and the dumbbells pressed together the whole way down. | Pause briefly at the bottom while still squeezing the dumbbells inward as hard as you can. | Press the dumbbells back up over your chest, driving them together even harder as you extend your arms. | Complete your reps, then bring the dumbbells to your chest, sit up under control, and set them down safely.

t: Stand tall on a low, stable platform or step, holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides with arms relaxed and your feet hip-width apart. | Brace your core, set your shoulders back, and fix your gaze forward to help you balance on the raised surface. | Step one foot straight back and down off the platform, lowering until that knee travels toward the floor below the level of your front foot. | Let your front knee bend over your mid-foot and your front thigh sink toward parallel, keeping your torso tall and the dumbbells hanging straight down. | Keep most of your weight through the heel and mid-foot of the front leg, using the rear foot only for balance. | Drive through the front foot to stand back up, returning the rear foot onto the platform under control. | Finish all your reps on one side, then switch legs and repeat for the same number of reps. | Set the dumbbells down safely once both legs are done.

t: Set a flat bench behind you and place a sturdy plate or low platform on the floor in front of it for your front foot to stand on. | Hold a dumbbell in each hand at your sides with a neutral grip, arms relaxed and shoulders pulled back. | Stand on the platform with your front foot and rest the top of your rear foot on the bench, finding a stance length that lets your front shin stay roughly vertical at the bottom. | Brace your core, keep your torso slightly forward, and lower yourself by bending your front knee until your front thigh is at or just below parallel. | Let your front foot's deficit allow the rear knee to travel below the platform for extra range, keeping your weight centered over the front heel and midfoot. | Drive up through your front foot until your front leg is nearly straight, keeping your hips square throughout. | Complete all reps on one leg, then switch the dumbbells and your foot positions to train the other side. | Step off the platform and set the dumbbells down with control to finish.

t: Stand a stride-length in front of a bench, holding a single dumbbell in the hand opposite your working (front) leg, arm hanging at your side. | Place the top of your rear foot on the bench behind you and set the working foot far enough forward that your shin can stay near-vertical at the bottom. | Brace your core and hinge slightly from the hips so your torso leans forward over the front leg — this is what shifts the load onto the glute. | Lower under control by bending the front knee and sinking the back hip down, keeping most of your weight through the front heel. | Descend until your front thigh is about parallel to the floor and you feel a strong stretch in the front-leg glute and hamstring. | Drive up through the front heel, extending the hip and squeezing the glute to return to the start without locking out hard. | Complete all reps on one side, then switch the dumbbell to the other hand and repeat on the opposite leg.

t: Kneel behind a stability ball with the ball positioned in front of your hips and thighs. | Slowly walk your hands forward and lean your torso over the top of the ball so your belly and chest rest across it. | Let your arms reach down toward the floor in front of the ball and allow your head and neck to relax. | Keep your knees or toes on the floor for balance, then gently roll forward until you feel a comfortable stretch through your back and along your sides. | Relax your glutes and let your hips drape over the ball so your lower back decompresses rather than holding tension. | Breathe slowly and let your body sink a little deeper into the ball with each exhale. | Hold the stretch for 20–30 seconds, staying relaxed and avoiding any bouncing. | To come out, walk your hands back, push your torso up off the ball, and return to a kneeling position with control.

t: Lie flat on your back on a mat with a stability ball resting just to one side of your hips. | Bend the knee closest to the ball and rest your foot flat on the floor for stability. | Keep the opposite leg straight, then lift it and let it cross over your body toward the ball. | Drape the crossing leg over the top of the stability ball so the ball supports its weight. | Keep both shoulders flat on the floor and let your hips rotate gently to deepen the stretch through the outer hip. | Relax into the position until you feel a comfortable pull along the side of the hip and abductor region. | Hold the stretch for 20–30 seconds while breathing slowly and steadily. | Bring the leg back over the ball under control, return to the start, and repeat on the other side.

t: Sit upright on the stability ball with your feet flat on the floor, roughly hip-width apart, and your knees bent at about 90°. | Brace your core lightly and place your hands on the ball or your thighs to control your balance. | Slowly walk your feet forward, letting the ball roll up your back until you are reclined and the ball supports your upper back and shoulders. | Keep your hips lifted and pressed slightly forward so you feel a gentle stretch along the front of your thighs and hips. | Relax your head and shoulders back over the ball, keeping your neck supported and your gaze upward. | Breathe slowly and deeply, easing a little deeper into the stretch on each exhale without forcing the position. | Hold the stretch while staying balanced, feeling the lengthening through the quads and hip flexors. | To finish, walk your feet back in, roll up to a seated position on the ball, and stand up under control.

t: Stand facing a wall, about an arm's length away, with your feet shoulder-width apart and your core lightly braced. | Place a stability ball against the wall at chest height and press into it with the heels of both hands, arms extended in front of you in a slight V (scaption) angle. | Push your hands firmly into the ball so your shoulder blades wrap forward around your ribcage (protraction) — this is the serratus engagement you want to keep throughout. | Keeping that pressure on the ball, slide it slowly up the wall as you reach overhead, letting your shoulder blades rotate upward while your arms stay in the V position. | Slide up only as far as you can without your shoulders shrugging toward your ears or your lower back arching. | Slide the ball back down under control to chest height, maintaining the forward press into the ball the entire way. | Complete your reps, then step back and lower the ball to finish.

t: Place a stability ball against a wall and lean your lower back into it so the ball sits between the small of your back and the wall. | Step your feet forward about a foot and set them roughly shoulder-width apart, toes pointing slightly out, so your knees will track over your toes as you descend. | Brace your core and stand tall, pressing your back lightly into the ball to keep it in place. | Bend your knees and hips to lower yourself, letting the ball roll smoothly up your back as you descend. | Lower until your thighs are roughly parallel to the floor, keeping your knees behind or in line with your toes. | Pause briefly at the bottom, keeping tension in your glutes and quads. | Drive through your heels to stand back up, letting the ball roll back down as you extend your knees and hips. | Finish by standing fully upright, then step away from the wall and set the ball down when your set is complete.

t: Start in a forearm plank: elbows under your shoulders, forearms flat on the floor, and feet about hip-width apart. | Brace your core, squeeze your glutes, and form a straight line from your head to your heels with no sag or pike. | Plant your right palm flat on the floor under your shoulder and press up onto that hand. | Push up onto your left hand the same way so you reach a full high-plank position with both arms extended. | Lower back down onto your right forearm, then your left forearm, returning to the starting plank. | Drive through each transition explosively while keeping your hips level and square to the floor. | Continue alternating which arm leads for the set time or rep count, then lower your knees to rest.

t: Set up in a high plank with your hands slightly wider than shoulder-width and your fingers pointing forward. | Brace your core and squeeze your glutes so your body forms a straight line from head to heels. | Lower your chest toward the floor under control, keeping your elbows tucked at roughly a 45° angle to your torso. | When your chest is near the floor, press through your palms as hard and fast as you can to launch your upper body upward. | Push with enough force that your hands leave the ground; if you have the power, clap your hands together at the peak. | Land softly on slightly bent arms, immediately absorbing the impact by lowering back into the next rep. | Reset your plank position if your form breaks, then continue for your target reps.

t: Stand tall and step your feet wide apart, roughly the length of one leg, with your arms extended out to the sides at shoulder height. | Turn your right foot out 90° so it points to the side, and angle your left foot slightly inward; keep your heels roughly in line with each other. | Bend your right knee until it stacks directly over your right ankle, with the shin vertical and the thigh working toward parallel with the floor. | Keeping your torso long, lower your right side and rest your right forearm lightly on your right thigh, or bring the right hand to the floor outside the foot. | Reach your left arm up and over your head so it forms one continuous line from your back heel to your fingertips, opening the chest toward the ceiling. | Press into the outer edge of your back foot, draw your belly in, and turn your gaze up toward your top hand if your neck is comfortable. | Breathe slowly and hold for 5 to 8 deep breaths, lengthening the side body a little more on each exhale. | To exit, press into your feet, inhale to rise back up to the wide stance, straighten the front leg, and repeat on the opposite side.

t: Sit or stand tall with your shoulders relaxed down and your spine in a neutral, upright position. | For the extension, slowly tilt your head back, letting your gaze travel up toward the ceiling until you feel a mild stretch along the front of your neck. | Hold the extended position for 15–30 seconds, breathing slowly and keeping your jaw and shoulders relaxed. | Return your head to neutral under control, then drop your chin slightly so your neck rests in a comfortable starting position. | For the inclination, slowly tilt your head toward one shoulder, bringing your ear toward it until you feel a gentle stretch down the opposite side of your neck. | Hold for 15–30 seconds, keeping the opposite shoulder pressed down rather than shrugging it up toward the ear. | Return to neutral, then repeat the inclination toward the other side for an equal hold. | Finish by bringing your head back to a centered, neutral position.

t: Set the bench to a moderate decline and sit at the lower end with your knees bent over the upper edge. | Hook your feet securely under the foot pads or roller so your legs stay anchored higher than your head. | Lie back until your torso is along the bench, keeping a slight bend in your knees and your chin gently tucked. | Cross your arms over your chest or place your fingertips lightly at the sides of your head without pulling on your neck. | Brace your abdominals and exhale as you curl your torso up, leading with your chest toward your knees. | Continue lifting until your upper body is well past vertical, keeping the movement controlled rather than swinging. | Pause briefly at the top and squeeze your abdominals. | Inhale and lower your torso back down under control until your shoulders return to the bench. | Complete your reps, then unhook your feet and sit up carefully to finish.

t: Load an EZ barbell and grip the inner angled portion with an underhand (supinated) grip, hands roughly shoulder-width apart. | Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart, knees soft, and pin your elbows against your sides with the bar hanging at full arm extension. | Phase one: curl the bar from full extension up to the halfway point (forearms parallel to the floor) and lower back down for 7 controlled reps. | Phase two: without resting, curl the bar from the halfway point up to full contraction at the top and lower back to halfway for 7 reps. | Phase three: again without resting, perform 7 full-range curls from full extension all the way to the top. | Keep your elbows fixed and your upper arms still throughout all 21 reps so the biceps do the work. | After the final rep, lower the bar under control to full extension and set it down.

t: Lie flat on your back on a firm mat or bench with both legs extended and your spine in a neutral, relaxed position. | Bend one knee and lift that foot off the floor, then place the outside of your ankle across the opposite thigh, just above the knee, to form a figure-4 shape. | Let the bent knee rotate outward and open toward the floor, keeping the ankle resting on the thigh. | Keep both hips level on the surface and avoid rocking your pelvis to one side. | Slowly lower the bent knee toward the floor, allowing gravity or a light press from your hand to deepen the hip and groin stretch. | Hold the open position for 20 to 30 seconds while breathing steadily and noting any tightness or discomfort in the hip or groin. | Bring the knee back up under control and slide your foot off the opposite thigh to release. | Return the leg to the floor, then repeat the same sequence on the other side.

t: Set two cones or markers about 5 to 10 metres apart on a flat, non-slip surface to form the loops of your figure-eight. | Start at the centre point between the markers in an athletic stance — knees soft, chest up, and weight on the balls of your feet. | Begin jogging toward the first marker, circling around it in a smooth arc rather than a sharp stop. | Lean slightly into the turn and shorten your stride as you round the marker to keep your balance under control. | Cross back through the centre and run a mirror-image loop around the second marker, completing the figure-eight. | Keep your eyes up and your core braced, pumping your arms in time with your stride to drive the pace. | Continue running the pattern for your set work interval, accelerating on the straights and controlling the curves. | Slow to a jog and then a walk to finish, letting your heart rate and breathing settle before your next round.

t: Stand tall with your feet shoulder-width apart, toes pointing slightly out, and place your hands behind your head or crossed over your chest. | Brace your core and pull your shoulder blades back to set a tall, neutral spine. | Hinge at your hips, pushing them back and letting your torso tip forward until you feel a stretch in your hamstrings, keeping a slight bend in your knees. | From the hinged position, bend your knees and sink into a squat, bringing your torso upright as your hips drop toward parallel. | Keep your heels flat and your knees tracking over your toes at the bottom of the squat. | Drive through your whole foot to stand up out of the squat back into the hinged position. | Extend your hips to return to a tall standing position, squeezing your glutes at the top. | Repeat for the desired number of reps, keeping the hinge and squat smooth and controlled.

t: Start in a high plank with your hands under your shoulders, body in a straight line from head to heels, and core braced. | Begin lowering into a push-up by bending your elbows and keeping them tucked at roughly 45 degrees to your torso. | As you descend, rotate your hips open and thread your right knee underneath your body toward your left elbow. | Keep your shoulders square and your supporting foot grounded as the working leg sweeps across. | Press back up to the high plank as you return the right leg to its starting position. | Repeat on the other side, threading your left knee toward your right elbow as you lower. | Continue alternating sides for your target reps, keeping each rotation controlled. | Finish in a stable high plank, then lower your knees to the floor to rest.

t: Sit on the floor or a mat with your knees bent and feet flat, sitting tall through the spine. | Place your hands lightly behind your thighs or rest your fingertips on the floor for support. | Engage your abdominals and lean your torso back to roughly a 45° angle, keeping your back long rather than rounded. | Lift your feet off the floor and extend your legs until your body forms a low, shallow V. | Lower the torso and legs closer to the floor so the legs hover just above it, deepening the abdominal engagement. | Reach your arms forward alongside your legs, palms facing in, keeping the chest open and shoulders relaxed. | Breathe steadily and hold the position, keeping the lower back from collapsing toward the floor. | To release, bend your knees, lower your feet, and sit back up tall before resting.

t: Begin in a wide standing position, turning your right foot to point forward and keeping your left foot slightly angled in. | Bend your right knee and reach your right hand toward the floor about a foot in front of and outside your right little toe, fingertips down or resting on a block. | Shift your weight onto your right foot and hand, then straighten your right leg as you float your left leg up until it is parallel to the floor. | Stack your hips by rolling your top hip open, and flex your lifted foot so the toes point out to the side. | Press firmly through your standing foot and reach your left arm straight up toward the ceiling, opening your chest. | Lengthen through the crown of your head and your lifted heel, keeping your core engaged and your spine long. | Gaze forward or, if balance allows, turn to look up at your top hand, breathing steadily. | To exit, look down, bend your standing knee, and lower your lifted leg back to the floor with control, then repeat on the other side.

t: Start on all fours or in a downward-dog position with your hands under your shoulders and your weight evenly balanced. | Bring your right knee forward and place it behind your right wrist, then angle your right shin across your body so the front of your shin lies on the mat. | Slide your left leg straight back, resting the top of the foot and the front of the thigh on the floor with the kneecap pointing down. | Square your hips so both hip points face forward and your weight stays centered, not collapsed onto one side. | Sit tall on an exhale to feel the stretch in your right glute and hip; keep your back foot pressing lightly into the mat. | On your next exhale, walk your hands forward and fold your torso down over the front shin, resting on your forearms or forehead as your hips allow. | Hold for 30–60 seconds, breathing slowly and letting the hips release a little deeper with each exhale. | Press back up through your hands, return to all fours, and repeat on the other side with the left shin forward.

t: Stand facing a wall and place both hands on it at about chest height for support. | Step one foot back, keeping the back leg straight and the toes pointing forward toward the wall. | Press the back heel firmly down into the floor until you feel a stretch along the calf and ankle. | Keep your hips square and your back leg straight to direct the stretch into the upper calf (gastrocnemius). | Hold the position and breathe slowly and evenly, letting the calf relax into the stretch on each exhale. | Hold for 20 to 30 seconds without bouncing, easing deeper only as the tension releases. | Release gently, then switch legs and repeat on the other side.

t: Start in a fighting stance with feet staggered, knees soft, hands up by your chin, and your weight slightly forward. | Shift your weight onto your standing leg and brace your core as you prepare to drive the rear (or lead) leg forward. | Pull the kicking knee up toward your chest, keeping the knee high and the foot cocked so the kick travels in a straight line. | Thrust your hips forward and extend the leg, pushing through the ball or heel of your foot into the target. | Keep your toes pulled back and your standing foot rooted, turning the supporting heel out slightly for power and reach. | Snap the kicking leg back to the chambered knee position immediately after contact rather than letting it drop. | Return the foot to the floor and reset into your stance with your guard up, ready to repeat or chain another strike. | Alternate legs or repeat for the prescribed reps or time, keeping a steady breathing rhythm throughout.

t: Stand with your back flat against a wall and your feet about shoulder-width apart, a step or so out in front of you. | Raise your heels slightly so your weight sits toward the balls of your feet, keeping your toes pointed forward. | Brace your core and press your lower back, upper back, and shoulders into the wall. | Slide your back down the wall by bending your knees, keeping them tracking in line with your toes. | Lower under control until your thighs are roughly parallel to the floor, or as far as you can go with good form. | Pause briefly at the bottom while keeping your back in contact with the wall. | Drive through the balls of your feet and slide back up until your legs are nearly straight. | Complete your reps, then step away from the wall and lower your heels to finish.

t: Find a straight line on the floor — a floor seam, a length of tape, or an imaginary line works well. | Stand tall at one end of the line with your feet together, eyes looking forward, and arms relaxed at your sides. | Step forward and place the heel of your front foot directly in front of the toes of your back foot, so they almost touch. | Shift your weight smoothly onto the front foot, keeping your torso upright and your core gently braced. | Bring the back foot through and place its heel just in front of the toes of the now-planted foot, staying on the line. | Continue walking heel-to-toe in a slow, controlled rhythm for the planned distance or number of steps. | Pause briefly on each step if needed to steady yourself, keeping your gaze fixed ahead rather than down at your feet. | Stop at the end of the line, return with control, and rest before repeating.

t: Kneel on a mat with your knees together and your shins flat on the floor, feet pointing straight back behind you. | Spread your feet slightly wider than your hips so there is room for your hips to sink between them, keeping the tops of your feet pressing into the mat. | Sit back and lower your hips toward the floor in the gap between your heels, not on top of them. | If your hips do not reach the floor comfortably, slide a yoga block or cushion under them so you sit tall without straining your knees. | Lengthen your spine, stack your head over your hips, and let your shoulders relax down and back. | Rest your hands on your thighs with the palms facing down and soften your face and jaw. | Breathe slowly and hold for 30 seconds to a few minutes, feeling the stretch across the front of your thighs and ankles. | To release, press your hands into the floor, lift your hips, and extend your legs forward one at a time to ease out of the pose.

t: Set a fixed bar, railing, or rack pin at roughly chest-to-waist height and confirm it is stable and will not move. | Grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder-width with your palms facing down and wrap your thumbs around it. | Walk your feet back until your body forms a straight line from head to heels, leaning into the bar at a steep angle. | Brace your core and squeeze your glutes so your hips neither sag nor pike up. | Lower your chest toward the bar under control, keeping your elbows tucked at roughly a 45° angle to your torso. | Stop when your chest nearly touches the bar, keeping your wrists stacked over the bar. | Press back up by driving through your hands until your arms are fully extended. | Complete your reps, then step your feet forward and stand up off the bar.

t: Stand facing a sturdy box or bench tall enough that your knee is at roughly hip height when your foot is planted on it. | Place one full foot flat on top of the box, keeping that shin close to vertical and your toes pointing forward. | Brace your core, keep your chest up, and shift your weight over the foot on the box. | Drive through the heel and midfoot of the top leg to push your body straight up, keeping the trailing leg relaxed. | Stand tall on top of the box with the working leg, bringing the trailing foot up to balance without slamming it down. | Pause briefly at the top under control, keeping your hips level and torso upright. | Lower the trailing leg back to the floor slowly, letting the working leg control the descent. | Reset your footing, complete your reps on that side, then switch to the other leg.

nE: High Hurdle Jump to Sprint and Cut
nR: High Hurdle Jump to Sprint and Cut
nH: High Hurdle Jump to Sprint and Cut
t: Set a single high hurdle and clear the space in front of it for a 5–10 metre sprint lane plus room to cut left or right. | Stand a short stride behind the hurdle with feet shoulder-width apart, knees soft, and your weight balanced over the middle of your feet. | Dip into a quarter-squat, swing your arms back, then drive both arms up and extend powerfully through your hips, knees, and ankles to jump over the hurdle. | Tuck your knees to clear the bar and spot your landing zone on the far side. | Land on the balls of both feet with knees bent and hips back, absorbing the impact softly rather than landing stiff-legged. | The instant you land, transition forward and accelerate into a sprint, staying low for the first few steps and pumping your arms. | After a few hard strides, plant your outside foot, drop your hips, and cut sharply in the chosen direction by pushing off that planted foot. | Decelerate under control, reset to the start, and repeat for your prescribed reps, alternating the cut direction.

t: Hold one rope handle in each hand with the rope behind your heels, elbows tucked close to your sides and your forearms angled slightly out. | Stand tall with your chest up, core braced, and weight balanced over the balls of your feet. | Swing the rope overhead by turning your wrists, not your whole arms, to start the rotation. | As the rope reaches your feet, drive through the balls of your feet and jump higher than a normal skip, bringing your knees up toward your hips. | Pass the rope under your feet during the airborne phase, keeping your jumps tall and your landings soft. | Land lightly on the balls of your feet with knees slightly bent to absorb the impact, then immediately rebound into the next high jump. | Keep a steady rhythm for your target time or interval, then slow the rope down and step out to finish.

t: Hold one rope handle in each hand with the rope resting behind your heels, elbows close to your sides and wrists relaxed. | Stand tall with your core braced, eyes forward, and weight balanced on the balls of your feet. | Swing the rope overhead using small wrist circles rather than large arm movements. | As the rope passes under you, drive your right knee up toward hip height and land softly on the left foot. | On the next pass, switch and drive the left knee up high, alternating knees with each rope turn. | Keep the rhythm quick and light, staying on the balls of your feet and absorbing each landing through the ankles. | Maintain an upright torso and steady breathing as you continue alternating knees for the set duration. | Slow the rope to a stop, lower your knees, and step out of the rope to finish.

t: Place the Bosu ball dome-side up on a flat, non-slip surface and stand a stride-length in front of it with your feet hip-width apart and your core braced. | Step one foot back onto the center of the dome, finding your balance on the soft, unstable surface. | Lower into a lunge, bending both knees toward roughly 90° while keeping your front knee stacked over your ankle and your torso upright. | Drive hard through your front foot and push off the dome to stand up explosively. | As you rise, drive the rear knee up toward your chest into a high-knee position, swinging the opposite arm forward for momentum and balance. | Control your descent and step the same foot back onto the dome to begin the next rep, keeping your movements rhythmic. | Complete your reps on one side, then switch legs and repeat, or alternate legs each rep for a continuous aerobic pace. | Step off the dome with control to finish, and reset your balance before the next set.

t: Start seated upright on the floor with both legs extended in front of you and your spine tall. | Bend one knee and draw that foot toward you, then guide the bent leg out to the side so the knee opens away from your midline (abduction) while the thigh stays flexed in front of your body. | Rest the outer ankle or shin of the bent leg comfortably on the floor or across the opposite thigh, keeping the knee relaxed. | Sit tall and gently hinge forward from your hips over the bent leg until you feel a stretch through the outer hip and glute region. | Hold the position and breathe slowly, letting the hip ease open a little more with each exhale rather than forcing it. | Keep the hold for 20–30 seconds without bouncing, staying within a comfortable range of motion. | Slowly come back upright, extend the leg, and release the position with control. | Repeat on the other side so both hips are stretched evenly.

t: Position yourself on a smooth floor in front of a fixed anchor such as a heavy table or couch legs, lying on your back with your knees bent and feet flat on the floor. | Reach your arms overhead and grip the anchor with both hands, using an overhand or neutral grip at roughly shoulder width. | Brace your core and press your feet into the floor so your hips form a straight line with your torso. | Keeping your body rigid, push through your feet and slide your body away from the anchor until your arms are nearly fully extended overhead. | Pause briefly at the extended position, maintaining tension in your back and core. | Drive your elbows down and back toward your hips to pull your body back toward the anchor, sliding along the floor. | Continue pulling until your hands reach your chest or your elbows are fully bent, whichever your range of motion allows. | Pause at the top for one count, then slowly return to the extended position under control to complete one repetition.

t: Position yourself under a sturdy, stable table with the edge at roughly hip height when you stand. | Grip the table edge with both hands just outside shoulder width, palms facing you or facing each other, arms fully extended. | Walk your feet forward until your body forms a straight line from heels to head, with heels on the floor and hips lifted. | Brace your core, squeeze your glutes, and keep your body rigid — do not let your hips sag toward the floor. | Initiate the pull by driving your elbows back and down while retracting your shoulder blades, not by bending your arms first. | Pull your chest up toward the underside of the table until your chest nearly touches or your elbows reach 90 degrees. | Pause briefly at the top and squeeze your shoulder blades together to maximize mid-back contraction. | Lower yourself under control back to the starting position with arms fully extended before beginning the next rep. | Re-brace your core at the bottom if needed, then repeat for the target number of reps.

t: Set a barbell in a rack or Smith machine at roughly hip height — the bar should be low enough that your arms are fully extended when you hang beneath it. | Place a bench or box a step or two in front of the bar, then sit on the floor and extend your legs so your heels rest on the bench at roughly knee height. | Grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder width with an overhand grip, arms straight, body forming a diagonal line from heels to shoulders. | Brace your core, squeeze your glutes, and keep your hips fully extended so your body stays in a straight plank throughout the set. | Initiate the pull by depressing and retracting your shoulder blades before bending your elbows. | Row your chest up to the bar, driving your elbows back and keeping them at roughly a 45-degree angle from your torso. | Pause for one count when your chest touches or nearly touches the bar. | Lower yourself under control back to the starting position with arms fully extended. | Complete all reps, then step your heels off the bench before releasing the bar.

t: Loop the center of a sturdy bed sheet around a door handle or through a closed door frame at roughly waist height, then pull both ends through to create two equal handles; tug firmly to confirm the anchor will not slip before adding your bodyweight. | Grip one end of the sheet in each hand and walk your feet toward the door until your arms are fully extended and your body forms a diagonal line from heels to shoulders. | Set your feet hip-width apart with heels on the floor and toes pointed up, creating a solid base. | Brace your core, squeeze your glutes, and keep your body in a straight line from heels to the top of your head throughout the set. | Initiate the pull by retracting your shoulder blades and depressing your shoulders away from your ears. | Drive your elbows back and down toward your hips, pulling your chest toward the anchor point until your hands reach the sides of your torso. | Pause for one second at the top with your shoulder blades fully retracted. | Lower yourself with control back to the fully extended start position over two to three seconds. | Complete all reps, then walk your feet back toward the door to release tension before letting go of the sheet.

t: Place two heavy, stable chairs back-to-back or side by side at a width slightly wider than your shoulders, and lay a sturdy bar, broomstick, or similar rigid object across the seats so it cannot roll or slip. | Sit on the floor between the chairs, reach up, and grip the bar with an overhand grip roughly shoulder-width apart. | Bend your knees and plant your feet flat on the floor directly beneath or slightly in front of your knees. | Straighten your arms and lower your torso toward the floor so your body forms a straight line from knees to shoulders — this is your starting position. | Brace your core, squeeze your glutes, and keep your body rigid as you pull your chest up toward the bar. | Drive your elbows back and toward your sides, leading the movement with your shoulder blades squeezing together. | Pull until your chest lightly touches or nearly reaches the bar, holding the top position for a brief pause. | Lower yourself under control until your arms are fully extended, maintaining full-body tension throughout. | Complete all reps, then carefully release the bar and sit up.

t: Set a bar in a rack or use a sturdy horizontal surface at roughly hip height. | Grip the bar with both hands just outside shoulder width, palms facing away or toward you, and walk your feet forward until your body is straight and angled below the bar. | Hang with arms fully extended, body forming a rigid plank from heels to shoulders, and let your shoulder blades rise passively toward your ears. | Without bending your elbows, actively pull your shoulder blades down and back — depressing and retracting the scapulae — until your chest rises slightly toward the bar. | Hold the contracted position for a full second, feeling the squeeze across the upper back. | Slowly allow your shoulder blades to rise again in a controlled manner, returning to the starting hang. | Repeat for the desired number of reps, keeping the rest of your body rigid throughout.

t: Stand between a set of parallel bars and grip each bar firmly with a neutral (palms-in) grip. | Press through your palms to lift your body into a straight-arm support hold, with elbows locked and hips neutral. | Allow your shoulders to rise passively toward your ears, letting your body sink slightly as the scapulae elevate — this is your starting position. | Without bending your elbows, actively depress your shoulder blades by pushing them down and away from your ears, raising your torso a few centimetres. | Hold the depressed position for one to two seconds, feeling the lower trapezius and rhomboids contract. | Slowly allow your shoulders to re-elevate and your body to sink back to the starting position under control. | Repeat for the desired number of reps, then carefully step down from the bars.

t: Position yourself under a bar or table set at roughly hip-to-waist height, then reach up and grip the bar with your hands wider than shoulder-width apart (wide grip position). | Extend your legs out and plant your heels on the floor so your body forms a straight line from head to heel, arms fully extended. | Brace your core and squeeze your glutes to keep your hips from sagging throughout the movement. | Pull your chest up toward the bar by driving your elbows back and wide, retracting your shoulder blades to engage the outer back and lats. | Lower yourself with control back to the start, then re-grip with your hands at shoulder-width or closer (narrow grip position). | Pull your chest up again, this time driving your elbows close to your sides to shift emphasis to the mid-back and rhomboids. | Lower under control to complete one full wide-to-narrow cycle. | Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, alternating or pairing the two grip positions each rep.

t: Stand with feet hip-width apart, holding a kettlebell in each hand with a neutral grip, arms extended at your sides. | Hinge slightly at the hips and bend the knees just enough to lower the kettlebells to mid-thigh — this is the hang position. | Brace your core and keep a flat back throughout the movement. | Drive through your legs and hips to initiate momentum, then pull the right kettlebell upward by driving your elbow high. | As the right kettlebell reaches chest height, rotate your wrist and catch it in the rack position with the bell resting on the back of your forearm and upper arm. | Lower the right kettlebell back to the hang position under control. | Immediately repeat the clean with the left kettlebell, driving the left elbow high and catching it in the rack position. | Lower the left kettlebell back to the hang position to complete one full alternating cycle. | Continue alternating sides for the desired number of reps, maintaining hip hinge and core tension throughout.
